faq.q: Is Budapest safe to visit right now?
faq.a: Yes — freely bookable. Hungary is US Level 1 (Exercise Normal Precautions), the safest tier, reissued 15 April 2026; the only everyday caution is pickpocketing on transport and in nightlife districts.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in Budapest?
faq.a: Not crime — the water and the money: the Danube runs fast, deep and cold (not for swimming), and the Forint invites dynamic-currency-conversion and street-exchange scams, so keep to crew-supervised boats and pay by card.
No — it is guided and beginner-friendly. Tours of the Palvolgyi and Szemlohegyi caves run 50-60 minutes at a constant 8-10 C with a guide; Szemlohegyi is a squeeze-free show cave good for families.

faq.q: When is the best time to cruise the Danube from Budapest?
faq.a: Late March to late December — spring and summer for terraces and baths, and late November-December for the Christmas-market sailings that make Budapest a marquee Advent start.

faq.q: Which river-cruise lines leave from Budapest?
faq.a: Nine confirmed — Viking, AmaWaterways, Avalon, Uniworld, Scenic, Tauck, Emerald, CroisiEurope and Riviera Travel — because Budapest is the eastern terminus of the classic Upper Danube itinerary to Passau, Regensburg and Nuremberg.

faq.q: Which Budapest thermal bath should I choose?
faq.a: It depends: Szechenyi (among Europe's largest, Neo-Baroque, City Park) for the grand day and the night sparty; Gellert for Art-Nouveau elegance; Rudas (16th-century Ottoman) for the Danube-view rooftop pool.

faq.q: Is Budapest a serious food city?
faq.a: Yes — it holds 7 Michelin stars (Stand at two), because a modern-Hungarian fine-dining scene has matured atop the classic table; pair a starred dinner with the 1897 Great Market Hall and a Tokaji or palinka flight.

faq.q: Can you run a marathon in Budapest?
faq.a: Yes — the SPAR Budapest Marathon (41st edition, ~10-11 Oct 2026) runs 6 distances from 5 km to the full 42.2 km along the Danube, sold as an entry-plus-stay running-travel package.

faq.q: Is the Douro Valley safe to visit right now?
faq.a: Yes — freely bookable. Portugal is US Level 1 (Exercise Normal Precautions), the safest tier, issued 23 December 2025; the only routine caution is pickpocketing in crowded Porto and on transport.

faq.q: What's the real risk to plan for in the Douro?
faq.a: Not crime — sun, water and the road: the terraces are steep and sun-exposed, the Douro is a dammed locked working river (follow crew on boats), and the N222 valley road is a tight switchback — use a driver or the Porto-Pinhao train, and never drive after tastings.

faq.q: When is the best time for a Douro cruise?
faq.a: Spring to autumn (roughly March-November), with September-October the harvest peak — you cruise past picking in progress and the quintas are liveliest, so harvest sailings book earliest.

faq.q: Which cruise lines sail the Douro from Porto?
faq.a: Seven confirmed — Viking, AmaWaterways, Avalon, CroisiEurope, Scenic, Emerald and Uniworld — because Porto is the single embarkation gateway for the ~8-day run up to Regua, Pinhao and the Spanish border.

faq.q: What's the difference between Port and Douro wine?
faq.a: Both come from the same Alto Douro terraces, but Port is fortified and aged in the Vila Nova de Gaia lodges (an 18th-century tradition), while Douro DOC is unfortified table wine — taste both, one at a Gaia lodge, one at a valley quinta.

faq.q: Where should I stay for a luxury Douro base?
faq.a: Two anchors: Six Senses Douro Valley, a restored 19th-century manor with a vineyard-heritage spa, for the valley itself; or The Yeatman above the Gaia Port lodges — 109 terraced river-view rooms, a two-Michelin-star table and a Caudalie Vinotherapie spa.

faq.q: Is the Douro good for a honeymoon?
faq.a: Yes — a quiet, high-romance wine landscape: a river-view quinta suite, a private terrace over the vines at sunset, and a Michelin dinner across from Porto's lit Ribeira. It reads couples, not crowds.
